question: An older patient seems to be losing their hearing, but it's actually a simple, fixable blockage. What is it?

question: What is the primary role of the cerebellum in the nervous system?

question: What is the key difference between inherited and acquired bleeding disorders?

question: Once a fat-soluble hormone gets inside a target cell, what is its main task?

question: In occupational health, what is the FIRST and best line of defense against workplace air hazards?

question: Why do we perform CPR on someone whose heart has stopped?

question: What is the primary medical purpose of inserting a flatus tube?

question: Why should you avoid pouring harsh surgical scrubs directly inside an open wound?

question: Which way of taking misoprostol gets into the bloodstream the fastest?

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of low blood potassium that a nurse should watch for?

question: A community health nurse visits a home where a mother has missed two vaccine appointments. What is the best first step during the visit?

question: When a blood vessel gets injured, what is the correct order of the steps your body takes to stop bleeding?

options.C: Vascular spasm, platelet plug formation, coagulation
options.D: Coagulation, fibrinolysis, vascular spasm

question: A client says they wore a condom inside out, flipped it, and kept going. What is your best nursing advice?

question: How does the body naturally balance out the forward pull of a growing belly?

question: Which of these is a major barrier that keeps Nigerian men away from maternal clinics?

question: Why does the electrical signal pause briefly at the AV node during a heartbeat?

question: As a nurse, what is an essential step when assessing a patient who might have a contagious infection?

options.A: Taking a detailed history of recent travel, occupation, and contacts
options.B: Isolating the patient in a surgical suite immediately
options.C: Measuring the patient's blood pressure every fifteen minutes
options.D: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics before checking lab results

explanation: You're building great clinical detective skills! Asking about travel, work, and who they've been around helps track down where the bug came from. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T3#GNS313_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which substance does the body overproduce during healing, leading to keloids?

question: How should a nurse respond when a community attributes an illness to traditional or spiritual causes?

options.C: Refuse to distribute any IEC materials until they change their religion

question: How do parks and tree-lined streets help clean up city air?

options.B: They absorb carbon dioxide and trap dust particles
options.C: They produce chemical gases that neutralize industrial smoke
options.D: They block all wind currents so microbes cannot travel

question: Why do biological males typically have a higher resting metabolic rate than biological females of the same weight?

options.A: They usually have a higher proportion of muscle mass
options.B: Their digestive tracts absorb fewer calories overall
options.C: They consume more water throughout the day
options.D: They have lower body temperatures on average

explanation: You got it! Because muscle burns more energy than fat at rest, having a higher muscle mass naturally bumps up the baseline metabolic rate. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h5)

question: Why do people with early cataracts often complain about blinding glare when driving at night?

options.A: The pupil refuses to open in the dark
options.B: Extra eye fluid spills over the cornea
options.C: Cloudy proteins in the lens scatter incoming light
options.D: The retina loses all of its cone cells

explanation: Spot on! Instead of letting headlights pass cleanly through, those cloudy clumps scatter the light everywhere, creating a blinding glare for the driver. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T4#GNS311_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is a leading cause of breakthrough seizures in patients with a known diagnosis?

options.A: Drinking too much water
options.B: Walking in cold weather
options.C: Eating green vegetables
options.D: Missed medication doses

explanation: Failing to take anti-seizure drugs as prescribed allows drug levels in the blood to drop, making a seizure much more likely. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h4)

question: What important advice should you give a patient given a 10-day course of antibiotics for strep throat?

options.A: Crush the tablets and mix them with cold fruit juice
options.B: Finish all the pills even if you feel completely better
options.C: Stop taking the medication as soon as your sore throat stops
options.D: Double the next dose if you miss a single pill

explanation: Spot on! Always encourage patients to finish every single pill. Stopping early can let the strongest bacteria bounce back and cause drug resistance. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h5)

question: You notice your clinic frequently runs out of single-use syringes, causing staff to reuse equipment. What is your best professional action?

options.A: Keep quiet so you don't upset the clinic manager during a busy shift
options.B: Buy plastic syringes from a local pharmacy using your own money
options.C: Stop giving all prescribed medications until the hospital closes
options.D: Report the shortage through official channels and advocate for safer supplies

explanation: Spot on! As a nurse, you have a duty to advocate for your patients and push for proper resources when safety is on the line. Great clinical leadership! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h9)

question: Lower national fertility rates are most directly associated with which public health outcome?

options.A: Guaranteed longevity past one hundred years of age
options.B: The elimination of chronic non-communicable illnesses
options.C: Complete eradication of all infectious diseases
options.D: Reduced maternal and child mortality burdens

explanation: Fewer high-risk pregnancies translate to fewer maternal and infant deaths, easing the strain on public health systems. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h5)

question: A patient develops sudden confusion and a high fever two days after surgery. What is a key trap the nurse must avoid?

options.A: Reporting the temperature change immediately to the attending surgical team
options.B: Reviewing the medication administration record for recent antibiotic changes
options.C: Attributing the symptoms solely to the primary illness without checking for treatment complications
options.D: Checking the surgical incision site for signs of localized redness or drainage

explanation: Spot on! Assuming every new symptom is just the original disease can blind us to hospital infections, drug reactions, or other unexpected complications. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following findings on an EEG report is considered abnormal and concerning?

options.A: Beta waves during active concentration
options.B: Focal spike and wave discharges
options.C: Delta waves during deep sleep stages
options.D: Alpha waves during quiet eye closure

question: Which test is commonly used to screen for too much adrenaline breakdown in a suspected pheochromocytoma?

options.A: Morning serum cortisol levels
options.B: Serum fasting blood glucose

options.D: Serum electrolyte panel

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four legal elements needed to prove professional negligence?

options.A: Actual damages suffered by the patient

options.D: Breach of the legal duty of care

question: What is the primary purpose of placing a drainage tube in a surgical wound?

options.A: To measure the exact blood pressure of the local tissue bed
options.B: To remove fluid or air and prevent dangerous accumulation
options.C: To deliver strong liquid antibiotics directly into the tissue
options.D: To keep the surgical incision completely open for daily inspection

explanation: Drains are used to clear out blood, serum, or air that can collect inside a body cavity, which helps lower infection risk and pressure. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h1)

question: Your patient looks nervous while you get ready to test their cranial nerves. What should you do first?

question: Who is the main target group for the preventive HPV vaccine?

options.B: Infants during their routine immunization schedule
options.C: Elderly women over the age of sixty-five
options.D: Adult men diagnosed with chronic prostatitis

question: Which patient position is most commonly used for a routine proctoscopy?

options.B: Prone flat on the abdomen

options.D: Supine with legs in stirrups

question: A relative has spent three days straight at the bedside without sleeping or eating well. What should you do?

options.C: Ignore the behavior since staying vigilant is completely normal

question: Why do fungal scalp infections like ringworm (tinea capitis) usually need oral medication instead of just medicated shampoo?

options.B: Oral medications are cheaper and easier for hospitalized patients to swallow
options.C: Medicated shampoos will permanently damage the texture of the hair shaft
options.D: Fungal infections on the head are completely unaffected by topical treatments

question: Which physical change points strongly to long-term high cortisol levels in Cushing's syndrome?

options.C: Permanent darkening of the mucous membranes and gumlines

question: What is the minimum number of days between periods that defines oligomenorrhoea?

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you accidentally suffer a needle-stick injury?

options.C: Apply a tight tourniquet above the injury site immediately

question: Which type of topical preparation is best for dry, thick, or scaly skin because it locks in moisture?

question: When nurses talk about 'pathological waste', what are they referring to?

question: What is a common challenge faced when gathering data in rural community settings?

question: A patient is worried about her changing body after a hysterectomy. Which goal fits best in her care plan?

question: Why is building trust with the community so vital during an Ebola outbreak?

question: Why must a nurse be extra careful when cutting the nails of a patient with diabetes?

question: What should a caregiver do first if a child swallows a toxic household cleaner?

question: What do we call a person who carries a disease-causing germ without showing any signs of illness?

question: How does putting perishable food in the fridge right away help protect health?

question: When is an exchange transfusion chosen over standard phototherapy?

question: A patient receiving an anti-bleeding drug suddenly gets short of breath and has chest pain. What should the nurse suspect?

question: You just finished soaking and washing your patient's hands. What is the most important thing to do before picking up the clippers?

question: Which finding at a pacemaker incision site should you report right away as a sign of infection?

question: What does prevalence measure in a community?

question: What do we call the practice of breaking a big ward workload into smaller tasks and giving them out based on staff skills?

question: What is the main reason a patient with acute viral hepatitis develops jaundice (yellow skin and eyes)?

question: What happens to the pupils of your eyes when the parasympathetic system is stimulated?

question: Why do healthcare facilities conduct regular fire and disaster drills?

question: What should you do when a patient suddenly falls silent during an emotional discussion?

question: A patient having a blood transfusion suddenly develops fever, chills, and sharp lower back pain. What is likely happening?

question: Why is the nurse so important during a patient's rehabilitation phase?

question: Why is it important to rest your fingers against the patient's cheek while holding the otoscope?

question: How does a nurse best show public health advocacy regarding breathing disorders?

question: Why is a Random Blood Sugar (RBS) test so handy in everyday clinic or ward work?

question: Which of these tasks is generally NOT okay to delegate to an auxiliary nurse?

question: Why is vigorous drying with a warm, clean towel so important right after birth?

question: In public health, what do we mean by 'food supply'?

question: What major nutrition paradox do we see in many societies today?

question: What happens if a nursing unit allows its stock levels to fall below the minimum safety threshold?

question: What is the main job of the intrinsic muscles found completely inside the tongue?

question: Why must nurses always take complaints of menstrual pain seriously?

question: What does medical confidentiality require of a nurse caring for an HIV-positive patient in Nigeria?

question: What is the main job of the accessory organs in our digestive system?

question: What is the main difference between microvascular and macrovascular complications in diabetes?

question: What is a major safety rule you must enforce when a patient is receiving oxygen therapy?

question: What personal protective equipment is a must when working in the CSSD decontamination room?

question: How should you think about a patient who comes in with general joint aches and morning stiffness?

question: What word describes an endocrine gland producing way too much hormone?

question: Which of the following does NOT happen during untreated status epilepticus?

question: Which food choice is generally NOT recommended when mixing crushed medication for an infant?

question: What happens during Active Range of Motion (AROM) exercises?

question: What happens when a primary health clinic consistently submits its monthly data late?

question: What does a 'narrow therapeutic index' tell a nurse about a medication?

question: Which of the following is a normal age-related change in the cardiovascular system?

question: What is a major cause of accidental needlestick injuries during injections?

question: A patient asks why they got a non-opioid cough syrup instead of a codeine-based one. What is the major benefit here?

question: In male patients, why must you push the catheter a bit further in even after urine first starts to flow?

question: What is the main purpose of a reflex arc?

explanation: Think of an antagonist as a stubborn security guard standing in the doorway—it sits on the receptor so nothing else can trigger it. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T6#GNS125_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is an early sign of fluid overload to watch out for during rehydration therapy?

options.A: Rapid disappearance of skin pinch elasticity
options.B: Puffy eyelids and swelling around the eyes
options.C: Extreme thirst and dry cracked lips
options.D: Sunken fontanelles in infants

explanation: Puffy eyes (periorbital edema) are a classic early warning that extra fluid and sodium are starting to build up in the body's tissues. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T18#GNS215_U6_T18_h6)

question: How do second-generation (atypical) antipsychotics differ in receptor action from first-generation drugs?

options.A: They involve both dopamine and serotonin blockade
options.B: They only affect the endocrine system
options.C: They completely avoid binding to any dopamine receptors
options.D: They act exclusively as serotonin reuptake enhancers

explanation: Think of second-generation drugs as having a double action: they block both dopamine and serotonin receptors. This unique combination helps reduce side effects compared to older drugs. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h1)

question: How does community-based care differ from hospital care regarding patient freedom?

options.A: There is no difference in personal autonomy between the two settings
options.B: Institutional care gives patients more freedom to choose their meal times
options.C: Community care relies strictly on hospital staff to dictate daily actions
options.D: Community care allows clients greater autonomy over their daily routines

explanation: Brilliant! At home, clients keep their freedom and call the shots on their everyday daily routines. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why is delegation such a helpful skill for nurses on a busy ward?

options.A: It allows nurses to manage workload by sharing routine care tasks safely
options.B: It prevents junior staff from learning advanced clinical procedures
options.C: It eliminates the need for any direct patient assessment by the nurse
options.D: It completely removes nursing liability from ward management

explanation: Delegation isn't about passing the buck; it's about teamwork! It helps spread out daily care duties so every patient gets timely attention. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h1)

question: What should happen to a palliative care plan as the patient's disease progresses?

options.A: It should be updated dynamically to reflect changing needs and wishes
options.B: It is handed over entirely to family members to manage at home
options.C: It must remain exactly as written on admission day to avoid confusion
options.D: It should be closed and archived once the patient becomes too weak to talk

explanation: Since palliative needs change constantly, our care plans must be flexible and updated regularly by the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h9)

question: In which dangerous condition should you NEVER give an anti-spasmodic medication?

options.A: Mild muscle fatigue
options.B: Seasonal allergies
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Paralytic ileus

explanation: A paralytic ileus means the bowels have already stopped moving on their own. Giving an anti-spasmodic would slow things down even more, which can be disastrous! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is a key nursing duty right after a patient finishes an MRI where they received mild sedation?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake for the next twelve hours to prevent swelling
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk briskly around the unit to clear the drugs
options.C: Monitor vital signs and level of consciousness until the sedative wears off
options.D: Perform a complete neurological exam every five minutes for two hours

explanation: You got it! Keeping a close eye on vital signs and alertness helps ensure the patient safely recovers from the sedative. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h6)

question: What causes the nausea and abdominal discomfort many clients feel right after drinking the GTT solution?

options.A: The solution is highly acidic and burns the lining of the esophagus
options.B: The high concentration of sugar creates an osmotic effect in the stomach and gut
options.C: Drinking cold liquid too quickly triggers an involuntary muscle spasm
options.D: The drink contains toxic chemical preservatives that irritate the liver

explanation: A hypertonic sugar drink draws water into the gastrointestinal tract through osmosis, often causing cramping, nausea, and bloating. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h8)

question: What happens to the ovaries when the brain's hormonal axis (the HPO axis) gets disrupted?

options.A: Immediate cessation of blood flow to the uterus
options.B: Premature depletion of all body fat
options.C: Failure to ovulate regularly
options.D: Permanent enlargement of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Spot on! If the communication lines between the brain and ovaries get scrambled, the ovaries don't get the proper signals to release an egg every month. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism behind a fat embolism following a long bone fracture?

options.A: Immobility causes fat cells under the skin to melt into the bloodstream
options.B: Infection at the fracture site turns local soft tissues into fatty deposits
options.C: The body stores extra dietary fat in broken bones during the healing phase
options.D: Fat droplets from the bone marrow enter open blood vessels and travel to the lungs

explanation: When a large long bone breaks, yellow bone marrow fat can escape into damaged blood vessels, creating emboli that block small vessels in the lungs and brain. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h6)

question: Why should you ask a patient about their alcohol intake when doing a blood assessment?

options.A: Alcohol increases the body's ability to absorb extra iron
options.B: Alcohol completely cures most inherited bleeding disorders over time
options.C: Patients who drink alcohol never need laboratory blood work
options.D: Heavy alcohol use can suppress bone marrow and impair liver clotting factors

explanation: Heavy drinking slows down blood cell production in the bone marrow and damages the liver, which makes it harder to produce clotting proteins. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T2#GNS311_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which piece of advice should a nurse give a patient to prevent food and drug mix-ups?

options.A: Take all medications with grapefruit juice to help speed up absorption in the stomach
options.B: Check with your healthcare provider before starting any new herbal or over-the-counter products
options.C: Crush all of your tablets together in the morning to make them easier to swallow with juice
options.D: Stop taking your prescribed medications whenever you feel completely back to normal

explanation: Always remind patients to ask an expert before mixing everyday supplements, herbs, or shop-bought meds with their hospital prescriptions. Safety first! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T4#GNS215_U2_T4_h7)

question: When is the best time for nurses to start teaching mothers about proper breastfeeding and preventing complications?

options.A: At the six-week postpartum checkup
options.B: During antenatal and early postnatal periods
options.C: Only after a breast abscess has formed
options.D: When the child is weaned to solid foods

explanation: Early teaching gives mothers the right techniques before any trouble starts. Prevention is always better than cure! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h7)

question: A patient with stable blood pressure keeps coming back, demanding brain scans because they are convinced they have a fatal tumour, despite clear test results. What is this called?

options.A: Health anxiety
options.B: Symptom denial
options.C: Stoic endurance
options.D: Normal recovery

explanation: When someone constantly worries they have a severe illness despite all medical proof to the contrary, it points toward health anxiety. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T9#GNS123_U1_T9_h5)
